title: Particles explained
summary: A review of the logical particles as a detective agency: が, を, に, へ and で each answer one question about the event.

blocks.text: **Logical particles** say how the parts of a sentence fit together: who did it, to what, where, with what. Each attaches to a **noun** and the pair stays together. Think of them as a team of detectives, each asking one question about the event. **は** is not on the team: it only flags the topic.

blocks.title: The detective agency
rows: Who did it? / what is it?
What was the action done to?
Where is it / where does it go?
Where did it happen? / by what means?

blocks.text: **が** is needed in every sentence, even when it is hidden. It is also the only logical particle that works in a **description** (A is B); the others work with action verbs. And a logical particle never changes its job.
You can **be** in a park (に), but to **do something** there you need で. で also marks the **means**: the bus you go by, or the language you speak in.

blocks.en: (I) go to the park by bus.
(I) speak Japanese. (Japanese is the thing spoken)
(I) speak in Japanese. (Japanese is the means)

blocks.jp: さくらとメアリーが歩いていた。

items: **が** doer · **を** done-to · **に** target / place · **へ** direction · **で** place of action and means.
**と** joins nouns and says nothing about the action.
Do not confuse the particles and they will not confuse you.
